questions.stem: Simple interest on ₹8000 at 6% per annum for 3 years is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 1 — direct SI. SI = PRT/100 = 8000 × 6 × 3 / 100 = 1440. Distractor 1200 forgets a year; 1560 uses 6.5%.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: At simple interest, a sum doubles itself in 8 years. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 2 — doubling under SI. SI = P means PRT/100 = P → RT = 100. R × 8 = 100 → R = 12.5%. For tripling, RT = 200. Learn the rule once — it covers 'doubles / triples / becomes k times' in one step.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% p.a. for 2 years is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 3 — CI via successive growth. +10, +10 → net +21% (using a + b + ab/100 = 20 + 1). CI = 21% of 10,000 = 2100. Trap 2000 is the SI value; 2200 double-counts growth.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: The difference between compound and simple interest on ₹5000 at 8% p.a. for 2 years is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 4 — CI-SI difference shortcut. For 2 years: diff = P(R/100)² = 5000 × (8/100)² = 5000 × 64/10000 = 32. Saves the full computation. For 3 years: diff = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: ₹8000 is compounded half-yearly at 10% p.a. for 1 year. The compound interest is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 5 — compounding frequency. Half-yearly → effective rate 5% per period, 2 periods. Amount = 8000 × (1.05)² = 8000 × 1.1025 = 8820. CI = 820. Trap 800 treats it as annual; 840 uses 10% simple.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A sum amounts to ₹4840 in 2 years and ₹5324 in 3 years at compound interest. The rate per annum is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 8 — ratio of consecutive amounts. In CI, A(n+1)/A(n) = 1 + R/100. 5324/4840 = 1.1 → R = 10%. The principal can be recovered next: P = 4840 / 1.21 = ₹4000.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Compound interest on ₹6000 for 2 years is ₹1260. The rate per annum is:
questions.explanation: TYPE 7 — back-solve rate. 1260 = 6000[(1 + r)² − 1] → (1 + r)² = 1.21 → 1 + r = 1.1 → R = 10%. Trap 12% comes from 6000 × 0.12 × 2 = 1440 ≈ but SI, not CI.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: At 5% p.a. simple interest, ₹1200 earns the same interest in 4 years as ₹800 earns in how many years?
questions.explanation: TYPE 1 variation — equate SI on two principals. Same R, equal SI → PT is constant. 1200 × 4 = 800 × T → T = 4800/800 = 6 years. Trap 4 ignores the principal difference.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
